No statement or choice requirement changed.

The imaginary scalar forms give Hermitian connections, curvature i dx wedge dy, and c1 difference d(-x dy/(2pi)); the witness and its unchanged Statement are valid. This is a nonfatal citation-restatement defect because the missing complex structure was already supplied in the proof.
The cited torus and Klein bottle square pairings both preserve their marked corners; their compact surface, Euler characteristic, and differing orientability conclusions remain licensed.

Both complex plane and punctured plane are connected plane domains, so their identity atlases satisfy the repaired definition. The exponential remains a holomorphic local biholomorphism with a noncompact fibre.

The changed Čech theorem clause concerns finite covers of the empty scheme; this counterexample uses a nonempty two-chart gluing and cites the separated comparison only for contrast, so its computation is unaffected.

F11 must retain the nonzero-ring convention of the dimension definition. Added it; all rings used in the dimension calculation are nonzero domains or localizations at the displayed prime. Also corrected the harmless description of h-t: its leading coefficient in t is -1, a unit, rather than 1. The map k[t] into k[x,y] is injective by y-degree, hence torsion-free and flat over the PID. Irreducibility follows because x^2(x+1) is not a polynomial square; the prime chain gives local dimension one while the quadratic relation leaves two cotangent generators.
The Frobenius fibre is nonreduced and hence not geometrically regular; the revised étale definition still implies smoothness, so the counterexample and its use of F8 remain valid.
The unit section of O_X has nonzero fibre at every point under the repaired nonvanishing-locus definition. Its global generation and failure of relative very ampleness are unaffected.

Spec L has one prime and dimension zero, so the rejected boundary assertion was false. Corrected it to distinguish the field cotangent dimension zero from the thickening cotangent dimension one. The s-adic orders in sg^p=f^p differ modulo p, proving s is not a pth power; Frobenius sends every polynomial in alpha into k, proving pure inseparability. The reviewed general theorem then gives the stated regularity and nonsmoothness witness, with no interface change.
The affine line is smooth of relative dimension one, with rank-one relative differentials; the corrected smooth-locus and fibre conventions still exclude étaleness.

L3 cites a topological definition for a local-ring assertion. The existing def-residue-field-scheme-point explicitly identifies the maximal ideal with pA_p; corrected L3 and its contract to cite it. Removed the unnecessary unsupported L4 attribution. In k[t]_(t), t/1 is nonzero since k[t] is a domain, and quotienting by t gives k. Thus reduction has a nonzero kernel, as claimed.
The closed immersion has zero relative differentials but is not flat; the repaired étale definition still includes flatness through smoothness, so the witness remains valid.

False positive in the declared page interface: library/pde/weak-derivatives-and-sobolev-spaces.md explicitly indexes coordinates x_1,...,x_n and basis e_1,...,e_n; its examples page imports these conventions. Thus j=1,...,n labels canonical coordinate j-1, and the n summands include every first derivative. Checked the full argument: p-q(n-p)<0 controls scaled bumps; L=h^2 gives critical gradient bound h^(2-n), and the core and annulus function bounds are uniform. No undefined nth canonical coordinate is evaluated under this relabeling.

The proof establishes the precise oriented Statement by integrating the zero curvature form and dividing 2pi chi=0 by 2pi. The title omitted the orientation qualifier and advertised a broader scope. Added oriented to the title; no nonorientable theorem is asserted or imported and the Statement and proof are unchanged.

The positivity supplier explicitly uses a choice-free finite-chart integral. Corrected A1 and 4.1 so AC is inherited only through global Gauss–Bonnet. Compactness gives compact support, nonemptiness and K>0 make K dA nonzero and positive, so its positive integral divided by 2pi gives chi>0. No classification is used.

The Statement correctly assumes connected and reduced geometric fibre, and its Artinian-algebra argument forces the global functions after algebraic closure to be the base field. Its inseparable degree-p example proves ordinary reducedness is insufficient. Corrected the title to state geometric reducedness explicitly; the claim and proof are unchanged.

A split surjection alone does not have zero residue kernel: k^2->k by projection is a counterexample. Repaired the local-freeness argument by first lifting a basis of N/nN, applying Nakayama for surjectivity, splitting by projectivity, and then applying Nakayama to the finitely generated kernel with zero residue space. This supplies the freeness used in 1.6; the Euler-Poincare cancellation remains valid.

The parent theorem and this corollary both assume full AC; the source locator incorrectly called that inherited assumption countable choice. Corrected the locator and A1 to include the parent local summation input. Setting every smooth subdivision turn to zero yields exactly the stated smooth-boundary identity, including empty boundary. No Statement change.

A map to Spec k has zero target tangent space, so the zero differential is surjective and remains allowed on V. Corrected the contradictory exclusion, the additional density denial (nonempty opens of irreducible X are dense), and defined the restriction g used in 4.1. Regular affine opens are smooth over k; the tangent criterion applies at every closed point, and the open standard-smooth locus has no nonempty closed complement by closed-point density. This proves all scheme-point assertions without changing the Statement.

The equality with dim X is a closed-point assertion; the generic point of A¹ has intrinsic tangent dimension zero. Restricted the conclusion of 1.1 to closed points and made the regular-locus existence argument on an explicit reduced affine spectrum. Closed-point density supplies a regular classical point, proving attainment of the lower bound. Automorphism stalk isomorphisms transport regularity, and localization covers nonclosed points without asserting constant intrinsic tangent dimension there. The Statement is unchanged.

The n>=2 energy proof invokes the first Green identity, whose Statement assumes AC_omega. Added that exact premise for n>=2; the n=1 mean-value and endpoint-normal argument remains choice-free. Zero continuous gradient energy forces zero gradient on each component and hence constancy. No direct item consumer exists; the home page already explicitly propagates Countable Choice.

The forward implication uses homeomorphism invariance; the reverse computes the same genus (2-chi)/2, including zero, or crosscap number 2-chi and applies classification to the same fixed model. The AC hypothesis is explicitly inherited from classification. No Statement/Definition or proof change was needed.

At a nonclosed t the combined fibre Jacobian computes Omega over kappa(t), so the old absolute-k claim was false. The intrinsic cotangent dimension makes the polynomial-minor loci agree on overlaps; classical projective projection is closed, and the parameter dictionary transfers its complement to a scheme open. Bertini and componentwise dimension drop produce a good tuple, and a form avoiding the finite zero-dimensional intersection proves r>d. The limit cannot be W1infinity because its k derivative is unbounded on positive-measure slabs. Checked the full/maximal graph limits using local weak stability and the finite-p jump witness using shrinking tensor tests. Statement unchanged.

A structure-sheaf section is not a continuous ring-valued function. In a local frame the nonzero fibre condition instead means the coefficient germ is a unit; a germ inverse spreads to a neighbourhood by the sheaf axiom. This proves openness without changing the nonvanishing set, positive-power convention or quasi-compact ampleness condition.
